title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
eligible_reason: Although the paper's identification is experimental (random access to Copilot, with IV/ITT estimates), Tables 3 and 4 also report a 'DiD' column that is a plain static TWFE of winsorized weekly outcomes on CoPilotInUse (a binary, absorbing indicator for having adopted Copilot) with developer FE and calendar-week FE, no controls. Adoption dates are developer-specific (staggered within each experiment) and never-adopters (control group and treated non-adopters) exist, so this column satisfies the Section 2 rules. Replication from the package is impossible because the shipped data are synthetic.
design_notes: Three developer-week panels (Microsoft, Accenture second experiment, anonymous Fortune 100 firm). runRegs: winsor2 outcome 5/95; DiD: reghdfe outcome_w CoPilotInUse, abs(id Year#WeekOfYear) cluster(cluster_numeric) [Microsoft], abs(id Year#WeekOfYear) cluster(id_code) [Accenture], abs(id t) cluster(team_code) [anon]; IV: ivreghdfe outcome_w (CoPilotInUse = ITT_afterXtreat); weighted IV via bootstrap; Poisson ppmlhdfe. Table 3 combines DiD/IV/Weighted IV across experiments (Combine_Table_InvVar_Weight_3.py) and adds an inverse-variance pooled column. Table 4 repeats for six Microsoft PR-quality outcomes restricted to weeks with TotalPullRequests>0. Coefficients are scaled as 100*b/pre-period control mean. README: 'the data in this replication package is synthetic data created for the sole purpose of allowing the code to run'.
main_or_robustness: robustness (DiD column reported alongside the headline IV estimates)
n_adoption_cohorts: developer-specific adoption weeks (not countable from synthetic data)

data_provenance: synthetic (README Data Note: proprietary firm data replaced by synthetic data; results from the package are 'meaningless')
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, ivreghdfe, ppmlhdfe, winsor2) with Python cleaning and table-combining scripts; ~11h runtime per README.
screener_notes: Eligible on a literal reading of Section 2 (the DiD column is a static TWFE on a staggered absorbing adoption indicator), but the authors present it as a naive comparison next to the experimental IV. Real data require author outreach (Mert Demirer, corresponding). The frame year 2026 and DOI mnsc.2025.00535 indicate a forthcoming article; check the cutoff rule. Screened from package only.
